import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset from CSV file
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a violin plot to compare the distribution of megapixels across different sensor types
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.violinplot(x='sensor_type', y='megapixels', data=data)
plt.title('Distribution of Megapixels by Sensor Type')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Megapixels')
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a bar chart to compare the average price of cameras with and without 4K video capabilities
price_with_4k = data[data['has_video_4k'] == 1]['price_usd'].mean()
price_without_4k = data[data['has_video_4k'] == 0]['price_usd'].mean()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.barplot(x=['4K', 'No 4K'], y=[price_with_4k, price_without_4k])
plt.title('Average Price by 4K Video Capability')
plt.xlabel('4K Video Capability')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between weight and price
plt.figure(figsize=(10,8))
sns.scatterplot(x='weight_grams', y='price_usd', data=data)
plt.title('Relationship between Weight and Price')
plt.xlabel('Weight (grams)')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
